evidence.details: Stage 1 name: ethyl [4-(morpholin-4-yl)-6-oxo-1,6-dihydropyrimidin-2-yl]acetate; patent [M+H]+ 268 and [M-H]- 266. CDX node 15 contains H/CR/N and a ChemDraw interpretation warning. Paired MOL has the known carbon-for-N error.
Sodium salt of the following stage: original CDX node 59 explicitly encodes Element=11, Charge=1. HN repair follows the preceding named intermediate. Original MOL shares the HN error.

Example 2 name N-(4-fluorophenyl)-2-[4-(morpholin-4-yl)-6-oxo-1,6-dihydropyrimidin-2-yl]acetamide; [M+H]+ 333 and [M-H]- 331. CDX nodes 15/29 each have two single bonds and inconsistent zero-H/invalid-valence annotations.

Table 1 compound A-4a: patent [M+H]+ 464. Nested fragment under node 70 contains N+, O and O- with one external connection. Restored full InChIKey equals paired MOL, including stereo: KCSNIJFTSPKGEI-XJRBWHPUSA-N.
Preservation control: source label tBu, direct attachment at the tertiary carbon; expected graph agrees with the paired MOL.
Example B131 explicitly names the methoxy substituent; final LCMS 420 agrees with C25H22FNO4 ([M+H]+ 420.1606). Source MeO attaches through oxygen.

Intentional single-molecule policy control. Expected selection is the protected Step 2 intermediate of Example 4-254, patent [M+1]+ 476.2; the final Step 3 compound has [M+1]+ 376.1. This fixture does not require returning all five document molecules.

Nested HO2C graph contains C=O/OH and one external bond. Paired MOL confirms the carboxylic acid and C=N geometry. After node expansion RDKit stereo caches must be refreshed from retained bond directions.
Original CDX explicitly contains three deuterium atoms (Element=1, Isotope=2) on N-methyl and a tetrahedral stereocenter. Unmodified RDKit CDXML and paired MOL agree on the complete isomeric graph.

CF3O has an internally impossible graph (three bonds on neutral oxygen; multiply bonded fluorine). Per scope, do not promote this ambiguous graph. This expected value preserves the old hydroxy output; it is NOT asserted to be the correct chemical structure.

H3CO has CH3 attached to both oxygen and an external point, implying five bonds on carbon. Do not promote it as a valid nested graph. The old hydroxy output is preserved pending a separate investigation; it is not a chemical gold standard.

A multi-bond T node is encoded as Element=1, Isotope=3. Treating it as tritium invalidates the graph. Its interpretation is deferred: preserve the existing query/scaffold result, without asserting that the [3C] placeholder is chemically correct.
Known missing CDXGenericList decoder in the pinned pycdxml dependency. The current work intentionally does not bypass or discard this property.

expected.error: CDXGraphicType should consist of exactly 2 bytes

evidence.details: Known one-byte GraphicType compatibility case. pycdxml handling is deferred; no global tolerance or property deletion is introduced.

Patent paragraph p-0040 explicitly defines T/U/V/W as independently CRa or N. The source nevertheless encodes U as uranium and V as vanadium. Preserve the old placeholder behavior; this is a compatibility control, not a chemically correct resolved molecule. After the user explicitly extended label support beyond R, the active assertion checks the independently read J/Z node labels. The original compatibility output is retained as baseline_expected; it is not a chemical reference. Ambiguous element-letter interpretations remain deferred.

Patent paragraph p-0227 defines J/K as hydrogen or leaving groups, including halogen/imidazolyl. Explicit Element=19 here is insufficient to infer potassium. Preserve the old placeholder behavior pending variable interpretation; not a chemical gold standard. After the user explicitly extended label support beyond R, the active assertion checks the independently read J/Z node labels. The original compatibility output is retained as baseline_expected; it is not a chemical reference. Ambiguous element-letter interpretations remain deferred.

Method 11 (heading h-0256 and paragraph p-1485) names the pyrazolopyrazine reactant and product. Node 159 is incorrectly Element=11, label Na, with an invalid-valence warning and one single plus one double bond in the pyrazole ring. Preserve the original N interpretation and both explicitly drawn structures.

The existing expansion/selection path chooses the bis-trifluoromethyl scaffold from this multi-structure drawing. Repairing another nested nitro graph changes the expansion decisions and exposes 14 components instead. Defer nested repair in mixed multi-structure drawings with unresolved dictionary abbreviations to preserve the current selection. This is a compatibility control.

Warned K+ is covalently drawn to tetrazolate N-. Preserving it directly makes RDKit 2025.03.3 create a dative K+ with seven radical electrons. Keep the original unresolved outcome pending coordination/salt handling; do not count that radical-bearing result as improved resolution.

Table compound A-503 has an N-methyl tert-butylpyrazole. Node 15 says Na/Element=11 but has an invalid-valence warning, a double bond and a single ring bond. Keep the pre-existing N repair; accepting the explicit sodium creates radical chemistry.

Scheme 12, paragraph p-0101 names (2-tert-butoxy-2-oxoethyl)(chloro)zinc. The nested ClZn graph instead attaches the external bond at chlorine, not zinc; RDKit silently converts the overbonded chlorine to a dative Cl->Zn graph. Reject promotion when sanitization rewrites source covalent bonds to dative bonds. Preserve the legacy outcome until this inconsistent attachment is addressed. The comparison uses the original baseline serialization directly: reparsing its query SMILES changes aromaticity and is not a lossless normalization.

The nested nitro groups are valid, but the surrounding N-ethyl triazole also contains a neutral ring N with one explicit H and four bonds. The legacy fixer can remove that H only before nitro promotion; a valid nitro N+ otherwise makes it attempt a negative H count. Defer promotion if it loses resolution rather than extend the approved zero-H repair to this different case.

Companion drawing to C02186, with excess H on a ring N. Keep the former output if nested promotion prevents sanitization. This compatibility result is not a chemical gold standard for the nitro intermediate.

Direct CDX text contains repeated R10 labels, some parsed by RDKit with atom-map 10. The labels must remain on their source IDs and must not enter the fragment-joining namespace. Paragraph p-0180 calls the reagent a vinyl stannane; low-valent tin chemistry remains deferred.

The source rings contain W1/W3/W4/W5 and Xb variables (Unspecified, no Element) with explicit 1.5 bonds. A variable electron count cannot define a unique Kekule form. Preserve the aromatic query edges and node labels; do not infer carbon atoms or lose the entire drawing. This is a query-graph expectation, not a complete-molecule gold SMILES.

Heading h-0055 identifies Intermediate 48 as dimethyl 3-aminopentanedioate. Paragraph p-0200 describes its synthesis and a 6H methyl-ester singlet at 3.56 ppm. CDX begins with a CO2Me abbreviation. The paired MOL/old reader incorrectly give one ketone and one ester.

The table row labels compound 1 as Fmoc-Ala (2-prime-quinolyl)-Val-OAllyl. The first source atom is the FmocHN abbreviation. Retained CDX stereocentres specify the dipeptide configuration. The old reader substituted methyl for the Fmoc-protected nitrogen.

Compound I-14 source drawing has a first-atom BocHN abbreviation in addition to another Boc group. The corresponding table row reports distinct 9H singlets at 1.52 and 1.54 ppm, supporting two Boc groups; the old reader and MOL lose the first one. Other bonds and the source stereocentre are retained.
